what_it_does: In large internet services, programs constantly call each other over the network using a protocol called RPC (Remote Procedure Call); this back-and-forth messaging has become one of the biggest hidden costs in modern data centers. A SmartNIC (a network interface card with its own onboard processor) can offload this work from the main CPU, but most SmartNICs connect to the server via PCIe — a general-purpose expansion bus that adds latency and has limited bandwidth. RpcNIC is a SmartNIC design built on a programmable chip (FPGA) that uses three techniques to shrink the PCIe overhead: batching outgoing writes into fewer, denser transactions; keeping as much data as possible on the host side of the PCIe link so the CPU's memory subsystem can access it efficiently; and dynamically adapting the encoding scheme when the RPC message format changes, avoiding redundant transfers.
